definitions.explanation: A fire made outdoors, typically for warmth, cooking, burning waste, or enjoyment. Associated with camping, autumn activities, and traditional Japanese winter scenes.

examples.japanese: ⟦キャンプ→キャンプ：03837_kyanpu⟧⟦{場|じょう}→場：03699_ba⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{焚|た}き{火|び}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{囲|かこ}んだ→囲む：02037_kakomu⟧。
examples.english: We gathered around the campfire at the campsite.

examples.japanese: {焚|た}き{火|び}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{焼|や}き{芋|いも}→焼き芋：15650_yakiimo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: We made roasted sweet potatoes over the bonfire.

examples.japanese: ⟦{住宅地|じゅうたくち}→住宅地：10158_juutakuchi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{焚|た}き{火|び}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{禁止|きんし}されている→禁止する：22145_kinshisuru⟧。
examples.english: Open fires are prohibited in residential areas.

notes:
WRITING:
Also written {焚火|たきび} or たき{火|び}. ⟦{焚|た}く→焚く：02285_taku⟧ is outside the standard kanji list, so the mixed and all-kana spellings are common in ordinary writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焚|た}き{火|び}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to have a fire going
- {焚|た}き{火|び}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{囲|かこ}む→囲む：02037_kakomu⟧: to gather around a fire
- {焚|た}き{火|び}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{消|け}す→消す：00528_kesu⟧: to put a fire out
- {焚|た}き{火|び}⟦{台|だい}→台：13039_dai⟧: a portable fire stand, standard camping equipment now that burning directly on the ground is discouraged

CULTURAL NOTE:
{焚|た}き{火|び} carries strong nostalgic associations with winter — the 1941 children's song 「たきび」 has children warming their hands at a neighbour's fire, with ⟦{焼|や}き{芋|いも}→焼き芋：15650_yakiimo⟧ roasting in the embers. In practice, open burning is now restricted in most urban and residential areas on fire-safety and air-quality grounds, so the word is met more often at campsites than in gardens.
